raw_response:
Forty-five years I have been doing this. I do not need anyone to tell me how to plant wheat and maize in Quzhou. My father did it, I did it, and I know what happens when you cut corners.

My land is 16 mu. Both halves work together — wheat goes in after maize, maize goes in after wheat. The whole field runs both crops, just at different times of year. Two people, me and my wife. We manage.

**Wheat — I plant it every October, harvest every June**

I buy the same improved variety I have used for the past several years. I do not remember the exact name but the seed shop in town carries it. Everyone around me uses it. My neighbor Wang got good yield with it three years running so I switched from the old kind and never looked back.

For fertilizer — I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I sow. That is 50 kilograms. Then when the wheat reaches knee height in spring I throw another handful of urea on top, about 15 jin per mu. I have done this my whole life. My yield is decent. I do not want to risk putting less because a failed wheat crop would hurt us badly. Better to spend an extra 20 yuan on fertilizer than lose 100 jin of grain.

Water — I pump from my well four times. Once before sowing so the seed has moisture. Once before winter sets in. Once at jointing in spring. Once when the grain is filling. If I skip the jointing water the stalks come out thin. I know this from experience.

Pesticides — twice. Early spring I spray for weeds, and at heading time I spray once more to keep the rust and scab away. Everyone around me does this at heading. A few years back my neighbor skipped it and lost a lot of grain.

I use my rotary machine to till before planting wheat, after I cut down the maize stubble.

**Maize — I plant it every June after wheat harvest**

Hybrid seed, always. I buy from the same shop. I do not touch traditional seed for maize — the hybrid gives me another 100-200 jin per mu compared to the old kind.

I do not till the field for maize. I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble. It saves diesel money and the soil stays better. My son-in-law in the next village showed me this a few years ago and I have not gone back to ploughing.

Fertilizer for maize — I apply one small bag of compound fertilizer at planting, about 25 kilograms per mu. Then when the plants are as tall as my chest, I throw urea again, about 20 jin per mu. That is the critical feeding time. The plants eat a lot right then.

Summer rain usually helps so I only irrigate twice — once right at planting if the ground is too dry, and once around tasseling time if August is hot and dry. Some years I skip the second one if it rains enough.

Pesticides twice — once right after planting I spray herbicide to kill the weeds before they get big, and once in the middle of the season if I see any worm damage or blight starting. Some years I skip the second time if the crop looks clean.

I expect about 470 jin per mu from wheat and 580 jin per mu from maize. That is what I have been getting the last few years. Nothing special but enough to cover costs and feed us.
